# Custom Pages Custom pages turn library data into your own dashboards, trip stories, maps, galleries, and other presentations. Each page appears on the **Pages** strip below the main navigation. A page with saved widgets opens in presentation mode; the pencil beside its tab takes you back to the design view that built it.
![The published Florida Trip page with a full-width hero and photo gallery](assets/custom-pages/custom-page-view.webp)
### Hero Widget A hero banner widget owns the whole width of the page: one photo, a heading, and a caption line. The widget supplies its own heading here, so the page needs no separate title bar.
### Gallery Widget A gallery widget sits under the hero with a count and a thumbnail grid. Each widget is a separate frame, so it loads, reflows, and can be replaced without the rest of the page following it.
## Create a Page Click **+ New page** on the Pages strip. Yaffo creates an **Untitled Page** immediately and opens its design view — an empty canvas with the page settings and the Assistant on the left. Nothing is published yet: a page with no saved widgets keeps opening in the design view, so you can come back and edit it whenever you like. A page with saved widgets opens in presentation mode instead. The strip can be folded away with **Pages ▾**. The fold is remembered across sessions, so if you cannot see any tabs, that is the first thing to open. ## Build a Page with the Assistant One sentence is usually enough. Yaffo picks widgets from its catalog, arranges them on the 12-column canvas, and keeps the result in a working version until you save it. AI generation needs a model and its API key — see **Settings** → **AI Generation** — and the steps below assume one is configured.
### Start a New Page Click **+ New page** at the end of the Pages strip. The new tab appears at once and the design view opens on an empty grid: **Title** still reads *Untitled Page*, the canvas has no widgets, and the Assistant is waiting with its example prompts. ![The design view of a newly created, still empty page with the Pages strip above it](assets/custom-pages/new-page-empty.webp) Name the page here if you already know it. The title is only written when you click **Save**, which is the last step. ### Describe the Page to the Assistant Type what the page is for into the box under **Assistant** — the occasion, the photos, and the shape you want, for instance *a hero photo across the top, then the rest of the beach photos in a grid below it*. Click **Send** when it reads the way you mean. Naming the photos, a place, or a year is what the widgets will select on. ![A description of the page typed into the Assistant box, waiting for Send](assets/custom-pages/assistant-description.webp) ### Watch Generation Run The canvas locks while the model works. **Add widget** and **Save** grey out, the message box and **Send** are disabled, and a **Generating…** bar appears with an elapsed timer. Widget headers keep only their order and size arrows, because nothing may be moved or removed mid-run. **Cancel** stays available. ![A design view with the canvas locked while generation runs, showing the Generating bar with its elapsed timer and Cancel](assets/custom-pages/generation-running.webp) The run does not need the browser. It lives in the working version on the server, so closing or reloading the tab does not interrupt it; reopen the page and the timer is still counting. ### Review the Draft When the run succeeds the draft becomes yours again. The grid unlocks, the widget headers get their pencil and **×** back, **Add widget** and **Send** re-enable, and **Save** goes live. Move a widget by its header, resize it from its corner, rename it with the pencil, or describe a change in the Assistant and send it — a follow-up re-runs on the same working version, not a new page. ![A finished draft in review: a hero and a photo grid, with the grid unlocked and Save enabled](assets/custom-pages/draft-review.webp) Nothing has been published yet. The published page, if there is one, is untouched while you work on the draft. ### Save the Page Click **Save**. On a page whose draft is ready, this publishes the working version and opens the page in presentation mode; on a page you are editing by hand, it commits the title, subtitle, tab order and layout and then opens the same view. The screenshot shows the hand-edited case, on a page created for this walkthrough. ![The design view of a page with one manually added widget, with Save at the left](assets/custom-pages/save-page.webp) Until you click **Save**, manual moves live only in this browser tab. Closing the tab before saving loses them. ### See the Published Page The page opens in presentation mode: the same grid, laid out the same way, with no editing controls and no frames around the widgets. If **Display title?** is ticked, the page title and subtitle appear above the grid. The tab is now active in the Pages strip, with a pencil beside it that leads back to the design view. ![The published page in presentation mode with its widgets and no editing controls](assets/custom-pages/page-presentation.webp)
## Explore the Design View
![The Florida Trip design view with page settings, assistant conversation, and two widgets](assets/custom-pages/custom-page-design.webp)
### Page Settings - **Title** and optional **Subtitle** fields; - **Tab order**, which sets the page's position among other custom-page tabs; - **Display title?**, which controls whether presentation mode adds a separate page heading above the widgets; - **Add widget**, **Save**, and **Delete Page** actions. Click **Save** to commit page settings and manual layout changes.
### Assistant Describe the page or widget you want, and the Assistant builds or changes it. [Read about generating a page](#generate-and-refine-a-page).
### Widget Controls Each widget's header has its title, a pencil to rename it, and **×** to remove it. Drag the header to move the widget. [Read about widgets](#work-with-widgets).
### Canvas The canvas is a responsive grid laid out on 12 columns. It reflows to six columns and then to a single full-width column as the canvas narrows, but **Save** always commits the 12-column layout.
## Work with Widgets A widget is an independently rendered block with its own title, data request, layout, and presentation code. Widgets run in isolated frames. Yaffo validates and resolves their library queries on the server, so generated widget code does not receive direct database or network access. Click **Add widget** to add a blank widget manually. Use its pencil to rename it, drag its header to move it, drag its resize handle to change its size, or click **×** to remove it after confirming. The header also carries **↑**, **↓**, **−**, and **＋** buttons that move a widget up or down the page and make it shorter or taller. They appear when you hover a widget, and stay visible wherever dragging is unavailable — on a touch screen, or on a canvas narrow enough to be a single column. The blank widget has no generated content; use the Assistant when you want Yaffo to design a functional widget. The Assistant can use or adapt these built-in widget patterns: - **Hero banner** — a full-width focal image and heading; - **Photo grid** — a simple responsive thumbnail grid; - **Photo gallery** — a polished gallery with captions and a lightbox; - **Library stats** — photo, people, and year summary tiles; - **Featured photo** — one full-bleed image with a caption; - **Filterable gallery** — a gallery with its own year filter; - **People** — person selectors and their associated photos; - **Photo map** — an interactive map of geotagged photos; - **Filter controls** and **Linked gallery** — a connected pair where filters update one or more galleries; - **Photo picker** and **Photo spotlight** — a connected selector and featured photo pair; - **Folder picker** and **Folder gallery** — a connected folder browser and gallery pair. This catalog gives the Assistant reliable starting points; it can combine, filter, restyle, or create other widget designs for your request. ## Generate and Refine a Page AI generation requires a configured provider and API key under **Settings** → **AI Generation**. 1. Describe the page or widget in the Assistant box and click **Send**. 2. Yaffo creates a durable working version and starts generation in the background. 3. While generation is running, the grid, Add widget, and Send controls are locked. The elapsed timer and conversation show progress. **Cancel** discards the working version after confirmation. 4. When generation succeeds, the grid unlocks so you can review, move, resize, rename, or request follow-up changes. 5. Click **Save** to publish the ready version. Closing or reloading the browser does not discard an active generation because the working version is stored by Yaffo. If generation fails, the draft becomes editable for a retry or follow-up, and **Save** stays disabled until a later run succeeds; a failed draft is never published. ## Present and Edit a Page Presentation mode shows the published version in a static grid without editing controls. If **Display title?** is enabled, the page title and subtitle appear above the grid. A widget can also provide its own heading, as the seeded Florida Trip page does. Open a page from the Pages strip. When its tab is active in presentation mode, click the pencil beside the tab to return to design mode. Manual changes to the published page remain in the browser until **Save**. AI changes remain in a separate working version until **Save** publishes them. This keeps a partially generated draft from replacing the current presentation. ## Delete a Page Open design mode and click **Delete Page**. Yaffo asks for confirmation and names the page that will be removed. Deleting a page removes its versions, widgets, and conversation, then removes its tab from the Pages strip. ## When a Page Will Not Build
### The Message Is Refused A notification naming a provider means no API key is saved for the active model. Nothing was stored, so the page is exactly where you left it: add the key in [Settings → AI Generation](../reference-maintenance/settings.md#ai-generation) and send the same message again.
### The Run Never Ends An elapsed timer that keeps counting is a run that is still going. Leave the tab if you like — the work continues on the server — or click **Cancel** and confirm; the working version is discarded and the page snaps back to its published version. If sending another message is refused because a generation is already running, cancel the run first.
### Save Stays Greyed Out **Save** is disabled while a run is active, and on a draft that failed. A failed draft is editable — move widgets, describe the fix in the Assistant, send it — but it cannot be published as it stands. Finish or cancel the run, then retry.
For how custom pages fit alongside filters, favorites, albums, and tags, see [Organizing Photos](../library-basics/organizing-photos.md). To restyle the whole app, including custom pages and widgets, see [Themes](themes.md).
files.description: The Custom Pages guide page: what a custom page is, creating one, a six-step guided walkthrough of building a page with the Assistant, an annotated tour of the design view, the complete widget catalog, generate/refine behaviour, presentation mode, deletion, and a diagnosis when a build will not finish.

Captures the eight screenshots of the custom-pages guide — the annotated published page and design view, and six walkthrough steps (new page, description, running generation with a frozen clock, draft review, save, presentation) — and drives creation, manual widget add/rename, save-to-presentation, the pencil back to design, and deletion through the confirmation dialog.

pageContext: Seeded states (docs fixture): 'Florida Trip' published (hero banner + photo gallery, 13 items, iframe titles 'Hero banner preview' / 'Photo gallery preview') — the design-view and presentation shots come from it. "Maya's Third Birthday" has a READY working version (hero + photo grid, iframe title 'Photo grid preview'): opening /design briefly enters the running phase (a READY startStatus still calls enterRunning), so wait for .page-design to lose `is-generating` before capturing. 'Chicago 2015' stays IN_PROGRESS forever with started_at 2026-09-01T12:00:00Z; unpinned the elapsed label read 67153:37. page.clock.setFixedTime(new Date('2026-09-01T12:02:41Z')) makes it read 2:41 and keeps timers (poll, 1s tick) running — install it before the navigation. While running: #add-widget-button, #save-page-button, #conversation-message and Send are disabled, Cancel enabled, #conversation-status visible with #conversation-elapsed, widget headers lose the pencil and ×. IMPORTANT: a running design page re-polls every 1.5s and reconcileWidgets rebuilds any changed widget's grid item, so every locator into a widget iframe can detach mid-wait ('Frame was detached') — all image waits go through withDetachRetry, and the Chicago gallery image wait is best-effort. Never click Save/Send/Cancel/Delete on the seeded pages. Every create/Save/Delete happens on a page the walkthrough makes, deleted again via POST /pages/<id>/delete with APP_CONFIG.csrfToken. The Pages strip (#navbar-pages-bar) is a server-persisted preference toggled by #nav-pages-toggle (PUT /pages/bar-visibility) and ships collapsed; the step-1 shot needs it expanded, so restore the found state in teardown. Still unverified: whether an AI provider key exists (assume none, do not send), and how the two .page-design crops frame at 1400px wide (the design canvas sat at ~860px inside a 1280px viewport, i.e. the 6-column band — check after a real capture). Step 5 ('Save the Page') illustrates the manual case on a throwaway page, because publishing a generated draft cannot be reproduced without a provider.
explanation: Read yaffo/routes/pages.py, templates/pages/{design,presentation,_grid,_widget}.html, static/pages/grid.js and db/repositories/custom_page_repository.py, then drove the sandbox to confirm the Pages strip and its three tabs, Florida's presentation (hero + gallery frames), Maya's READY draft (Save enabled, Cancel disabled), and Chicago's locked running state whose unpinned timer read 67153:37 and read a stable 2:41 once page.clock.setFixedTime froze Date.now at 2026-09-01T12:02:41Z. That set the plan: annotated screenshots for the two views the prose explains, and a six-step guide-walkthrough for the Assistant build with the running step from Chicago, the review step from Maya, and create/describe/save on a page this walkthrough creates and deletes. The first capture failed because grid.js reconciles each polled widget change by rebuilding the grid item, detaching the iframe the image wait was inside; the fix keeps the same shots and routes but wraps every frame wait in a detach-retry helper that re-resolves the locator against the rebuilt frame, and makes the running-state gallery wait explicitly best-effort so a 1.5s poll cannot fail the capture. Confidence stays moderate because I could not view the captured images and could not confirm whether an AI provider key exists.
